segments.translation_text: The rupakaya of all the Buddhas Is born from the perfect accumulation of merit; O King, in short, the dharmakaya Is born from the accumulation of primordial wisdom.
segments.source_html: སངས་རྒྱས་རྣམས་ཀྱི་གཟུགས་ཀྱི་སྐུ། ། བསོད་ནམས་ཚོགས་ལས་ཡང་དག་འཁྲུངས། ། ཆོས་ཀྱི་སྐུ་དེ་མདོར་བསྡུ་ན། རྒྱལ་པོ་ཡེ་ཤེས་ཚོགས་ལས་འཁྲུངས། [p.-20][[རབ་གསལ་སྣང་བ་]]
segments.translation_html:
The rupakaya of all the Buddhas
Is born from the perfect accumulation of merit;
O King, in short, the dharmakaya
Is born from the accumulation of primordial wisdom.

segments.translation_text: When the time arrived to tame beings in the realm of Jambudivipa, he passed the jeweled crown to the Bodhisattva Maitreya, designating him as his regent. He announced to the gods, "I now embark for the human realm in order to tame beings there. The invincible Bodhisattva Maitreya shall teach you the holy Dharma. Dwell heedful of the doctrine. When I turn the wheel of Dharma in Jambudivipa, come to receive the teachings there.” With these words, he gradually descended. This is known as the deed of transference from Dushita heaven.

When I turn the wheel of Dharma in Jambudivipa, come to receive the teachings there.” With these words, he gradually descended. This is known as the deed of transference from Dushita heaven.

segments.translation_text: Then he assumed an emanation body as described in the Brahman Vedas. As a very white elephant with six tusks, back caparisoned with tassels of gold, he entered his mother’s body through her right side while she dwelt in observance of posadha vows. Inconceivable auspicious signs occurred, and his mother’s womb was blessed as a celestial mansion configured as a jewel. Thus for ten months he dwelt in bliss. This is known as the deed of entering the mother’s womb.

segments.translation_text: At the age of fifteen, in order to continue the family lineage, he was requested to accept a princess who possessed special good qualities. Shakya Dandapani, the father of the chosen maiden, and other fathers announced a contest in the peaceful and martial arts and offered their daughters to the winner as a prize. Devadatta and many other youths heard of the competition and gathered to enter the events in literature, mathematics, running, jumping, and archery. The Bodhisattva was the winner of every event. He accepted as his princesses Gopa, Yasodhara, and the other maidens Sujata, and Deer Holder, each with a retinue of twenty thousand attendants. This is known as the deed of enjoying a queen and retinue.

segments.translation_html: In order to defeat heretics who believed it possible to obtain liberation through practicing inferior behavior as exalted method such as dwelling naked, carrying a trident, sitting surrounded by five fires and other austerities, for six years the Bodhisattva performed many different types of equipoise meditation in a cove of the Nairanjana River. Through unwavering samadhi that stops exhalation and inhalation, and taking only a half grain of sesame seed in place of food, his body became dried and emaciated.

segments.translation_text: The Bodhisattva proceeded to Bodhigaya, bound for the holy place where many previous Buddhas attained enlightenment. On the road, a grass seller named Mangala offered sweet smelling kusa grass as iridescent and smooth as a peacock’s neck. The Bodhisattva accepted it as his cushion, arranging it in a straight pattern in front of the Bodhi tree. Upon it, he sat facing the east, with his body in full meditation posture and resolved, "Here I shall remain without wavering until I reach unsurpassable enlightenment.’’ All the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas sang songs of praise and veneration. This deed is known as approaching the essence of enlightenment.

segments.translation_text: Advancing toward the Buddha, they threw a ceaseless hailstorm of weapons: mountains, rocks, fire, lightning, weapon wheels, spears, swords, clubs, and arrows. Thus, the forces of mara were completely unable to disturb the Bodhisattva by the manifestation of anger.

segments.translation_text: In the early part of the night, the Bodhisattva actualized the four dhyana; at midnight, he developed clairvoyance; and at dawn, he manifested the state of exhaustion of all contamination. segments.translation_text: Knowing that he had temporarily completed the work of benefiting disciples in this realm; to encourage lazy ones to be diligent in the practice of Dharma; to reject the wrong views of those who believe in permanence; and for a multitude of other reasons, the Buddha traveled to Kushinagara, where between two sala trees, he reclined upon his last bed. segments.translation_text: According to some explanations, the Buddha has four kaya, or bodies. For one’s own purpose, there are two: the swabavakaya which is doubly pure, and the dharmakaya which is the ultimate state of primordial wisdom. In different terms, these are also known as the great bliss aspect and emptiness aspect respectively. The two can also be considered as one, and thus this categorization does not contradict an explanation of three kaya.

segments.translation_text: With regard to both teacher and disciple, the practice of giving is: performing the preparations; possessing enlightenment thought; timeliness; bestowing Dharma teaching; offering tokens of appreciation for it; and other activities. segments.translation_html: Miyowade warned the king, "You will not be able to bear the sight of my sword.” However, the king repeatedly ordered him to present it. Finally Miyowade consented, saying to the king, "In that case, please retire to an isolated room, cover one eye, and look with the other eye.” The king did so. When Miyowade pulled the wooden sword from the case, it was so awesomely dazzling that one of the king’s eyes fell to the floor. His retinue and guards were completely terrified, and begged for protection. Miyowade picked up the king’s eye, returned it to the king’s eye socket, and blessed it so that there would be no pain.

segments.translation_text: Other earlier masters explain that the first two verses demonstrate that one should not waste the opportunity of having this human body with leisure and endowment, and advice to make this life meaningful. The first chapter explains how to engage in enlightenment thought. The second and third chapters explain how to develop that enlightenment thought. Then, having generated enlightenment thought, the fourth and fifth chapters show how to guard the precepts in order that they will not decline. What needs to be guarded is the six perfections, which are the nature of the precepts. Out of these six, the first two need to be realized based on the first five chapters. The last four chapters can be understood from their respective titles.

segments.translation_html:
Just as a flash of lightning on a dark, cloudy night
For an instant brightly illuminates all,
Likewise, occasionally by the power of the Buddha,
A rare virtuous thought occurs in the world.

segments.translation_text: During the night, which is without the sun; in darkness, which is without the moon; under dense clouds, which obscure even the light of the stars, if lightning suddenly flashes, physical objects are momentarily illuminated. Similarly, for one in a hundred beings dwelling in the darkness of samsara, by the power of the light of compassion of the Bhagwan Buddhas, a wish to engage in the holy Dharma for the purpose of themself and other beings may occur. Such a virtuous light of the mind occurs only rarely, and even if it occurs, it does not last long. Therefore, having found this thought, it is right to engage in the conduct of great beings. The Essence of Madhyamika states:
